dialogue.content: Any tips for storing undeveloped rolls so they do not get ruined in a warm apartment?
Keep them in a sealed bag in the fridge if you will wait more than a couple of weeks, and let them warm up before opening to avoid condensation.
People keep telling me gear upgrades are worth it. I am skeptical.
Upgrades help only when a specific limitation is blocking you. Otherwise they mostly spend money and attention.
I have been developing rolls at home lately. My hobby spending is basically frozen until April, so I am not buying any new equipment before then.
Working within a freeze is a solid constraint. Home developing plus what you already own can carry you until April without new purchases.
Is there a cheap way to scan negatives that does not look terrible?
A simple light pad plus a phone clamp can look surprisingly good if you keep dust down and shoot RAW. Dedicated scanners can wait.
Weekday evenings I am stuck indoors. The only outdoor shooting window I really get is Saturday and Sunday mornings, and even then the winter light dies early.
That makes weekend mornings your scarce resource. Protecting those hours matters more than collecting more tools.
A friend said a midweek coastal outing with fancy kit would be amazing. I have not answered yet.
No rush. Check whether the timing and cost fit your actual constraints before you commit.
How do I tell if a trip invitation is actually aligned with my hobbies versus just FOMO?
Ask what concrete practice it enables that you cannot do at home. If the answer is vague prestige, it is probably FOMO.
I compared two more options and kept the details.
That gives you another detail to weigh against your priorities.
Okay, deciding now. Someone offered a Wednesday coastal outing with a borrowed high-end body. Is that a smart move for me right now?
